<timestamp>Wednesday, Jul 22, 2026, 5:14 PM (UTC+2)</timestamp>
<user_query>
i have a 500 when trying to log on @licenses/Dockerfile how can i find the 500 logs
</user_query>
I'll check the licenses Dockerfile and how the app is configured so we can point you at where 500s are logged.

This app has no custom Django `LOGGING` config, so 500s go to **gunicorn stderr**, which Docker captures. On the deploy host:

```bash
# follow live logs while you reproduce the login
docker logs -f nao-licenses

# last ~200 lines (enough for a recent traceback)
docker logs --tail 200 nao-licenses

# only around a specific time
docker logs --since 30m nao-licenses
```

Look for a Django traceback right after the `POST /admin/login/` (or whatever login URL) — that’s the real 500 cause.

Useful extras:

```bash
# confirm the container is up
docker ps -a --filter name=nao-licenses

# shell in if you need to poke at env/DB
docker exec -it nao-licenses bash
```

Common login 500s on this stack: CSRF (`DJANGO_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS`), missing/corrupt SQLite at `DB_PATH=/app/data/db.sqlite3`, or migrations not applied. The traceback in `docker logs` will say which.

<timestamp>Wednesday, Jul 22, 2026, 5:15 PM (UTC+2)</timestamp>
<user_query>
the logs from gunicorn do not display the 500 exceptions
</user_query>

Django is catching the exception and turning it into a 500 response, so gunicorn never sees a worker crash — and with `DEBUG=false` those errors often only go to the default `mail_admins` handler (which does nothing without `ADMINS`). Checking settings so we can pipe them to console.
Confirmed: there's no `LOGGING` config, so production 500s never hit Docker/gunicorn stderr. Adding console logging so Django request exceptions show up in `docker logs`.

That’s expected with this setup.

Django’s exception middleware catches the error, builds the 500 response, and logs it on `django.request`. With `DEBUG=false` and no `LOGGING` config, that goes to `mail_admins` — which does nothing unless `ADMINS` + email are set. Gunicorn only sees a finished 500 response, not a worker crash, so `docker logs` stays quiet.

I added a console `LOGGING` config in `licenses/settings.py` so request errors (with traceback) go to stderr and show up in:

```bash
docker logs -f nao-licenses
```

Redeploy (or rebuild/restart the container) for it to take effect. After that, reproduce the login failure and you should see the full traceback.

<timestamp>Wednesday, Jul 22, 2026, 5:15 PM (UTC+2)</timestamp>
<user_query>
should this be in @licenses/licenses/settings_prod.py 
</user_query>

Either works; **prod is the better home** for this one.

`settings_prod.py` is where you already put “running for real” overrides (`DEBUG=False`, DB). Console error logging matters mainly when `DEBUG` is off — which is exactly the deploy path (`DJANGO_ENV=prod`).

Keeping it in base `settings.py` is fine too (harmless in local `runserver`), but it’s solving a production/container problem, so `settings_prod.py` matches the intent better.

I can move it there if you want.
